**10:15 – Rachel Adams**

I'd recommend a visual inspection within the next week to check for any loose connections. I can schedule it for next Tuesday if that suits.

Thanks Rachel. Tuesday works for us – I'll add it to the inspection roster. Let me know if you need any track access arranged.

documents.content:
**Thread: Ballarat Soft Spot – Geotech Follow-up**

**09:40 – Priya Sharma** (Thursday 16 July)
Geotech crew arrived on site at 08:30. They've done the boreholes and a couple of test pits along the affected section. Initial read is that the soft spot is confined to the top 300 mm and the subgrade below is sound. They're packing up now and will have the written report to me by Friday COB.

**09:45 – Rachel Adams**
Good to hear. Does that mean we can lift the 60 km/h restriction sooner than Friday? The 4-minute delay is still holding but it's been a week now and the local member's office has asked twice about when normal running will resume.

**09:50 – Priya Sharma**
Not until I see the written recommendation. The verbal advice is positive but I'm not comfortable lifting a speed restriction on a verbal. I'll circulate the report as soon as it lands and we can make the call then.

**10:05 – Dana Whitfield**
Fair enough. I'll keep the night shift doing the visual checks until we get the all clear. The dip hasn't changed overnight – still settled, no fresh cracking.

---

**Thread: Ararat–Ballarat Line – July Closure – Post-Closure Inspection**

**07:30 – Dana Whitfield** (Thursday 16 July)
Post-closure inspection complete. Track geometry through the closed section is within tolerance. The new ballast on the approach to Buangor has settled well. One item – the top of the rail on the down line at the Ararat end has a slight surface irregularity about 200 mm long. It's not a defect under the standards but I've flagged it for the next grinding cycle.

**07:35 – Priya Sharma**
Thanks Dana. I'll add the rail grinding note to the August planning list. Anything else from the closure?

**07:40 – Dana Whitfield**
Signal room access at Ararat went smoothly. The key handover was on time and the room was left secure. The only hiccup was the generator – it wouldn't start when we tested it before the possession, but we had the backup unit from the depot so no impact. I'll log it for maintenance.

**07:45 – Rachel Adams**
I'll chase the generator maintenance ticket. Also, the MTS access requirements doc has been updated to reflect the approved possession. No further action needed there.

---

**Thread: Geelong Line – Level Crossing Warning System – Monday 20 July**

**10:00 – Marcus Chen** (Friday 17 July)
Quick update on the level crossing warning system at the Bannockburn road crossing. The fault logged on Wednesday – intermittent activation with no train present – has been traced to a faulty track circuit connection. The signalling crew has replaced the connection and the system has been in test mode since 08:00 this morning. No false activations since. I'd like to keep it in test mode over the weekend and do a final verification on Monday before we return it to normal service.

**10:05 – Priya Sharma**
Agreed. Keep it in test mode and do the verification first thing Monday. Who's on the signallers' roster for Monday?

**10:10 – Marcus Chen**
Tom Bell is on shift from 06:00. He's familiar with the site – he did the original install two years ago. I'll have him do the verification and sign it off.

**10:15 – Rachel Adams**
I'll note the test mode in the network status page so the customer service team knows what to say if anyone reports an issue over the weekend.

---

**Thread: Ballarat Soft Spot – Geotech Report Received**

**15:20 – Priya Sharma** (Friday 17 July)
Geotech report is in. Summary: the soft spot is a localised surface issue caused by drainage water pooling under the ballast. The subgrade is sound. Recommendation is to lift the 60 km/h restriction and monitor with weekly visual checks for the next month. A permanent drainage fix is recommended as part of the next capital works program.
